levels.title: First words
levels.goal: Single words and short phrases for your first days in Lebanon.

items.note: The reply is 'ahla fik' to a man, 'ahla fike' to a woman.
Reply with 'sabe7 l nour' (morning of light).
Lebanese changes the ending depending on who you're talking to.
This one follows the speaker: a woman says 'mni7a' about herself.
The most common answer to 'kifak?', whatever your religion.

lessons.title: Who are you?
lessons.subtitle: Names, where you're from, and getting by

items.note: Literally 'and me more'. The standard reply to 'tsharrafna'.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.english: I'm Maya. Where are you from?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.arabic: أنا من كندا. عم بتعلّم عربي.
dialogue.english: I'm from Canada. I'm learning Arabic.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.english: Little by little... nice to meet you!

'hayda' for a man, 'hayde' for a woman.

lessons.title: At the café
lessons.subtitle: Order a coffee and pay the bill

items.note: In Beirut the 'q' sound drops out: 'ahwe', not 'qahwe'.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.english: Medium sugar. And a glass of water.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.english: Thanks. The bill, please. How much?

lessons.title: Days & time
lessons.subtitle: Today, tomorrow, and what time it is

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.english: OK, I have to go. See you tomorrow?

levels.title: First sentences
levels.goal: Your first full sentences: want, have, like, can, need.

items.note: Put 'ma' in front to say no.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.arabizi: Sam, ana jou3ane. fi shi nekol?
dialogue.arabic: سام، أنا جوعانة. في شي ناكل؟
dialogue.english: Sam, I'm hungry. Is there anything to eat?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.arabizi: eh, fi man2ouche. bas ma 3ande wa2t.
dialogue.arabic: إيه، في منقوشة. بس ما عندي وقت.
dialogue.english: Yes, there's man'oushe. But I don't have time.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.english: I want to go home now.
